headline: 5 FIRMS, 3 SITES
NORDIC AI **BID**
cover.hook_pick_reason: Names the bid and gives two numbers that slides 2 and 3 back up: five companies in the group and three confirmed sites (Oulu, Iru, Valmiera; Sweden is undecided, slide 3). It promises no approval or funding. The rivalry option puts Nokia against Telekom, but heise says Telekom is only among the most prominent rivals and the group is not led by Nokia alone (slide 6), so it overstates. 'Goes north' is vaguer and has no number. No reader-impact hook: the article states no effect on ordinary readers (what they pay, use or risk); it covers an industry bid for EU funding.

slides.title: Five firms eye EU AI funding
body: Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda formed a consortium, **AI Gigafactory Northern**. The group plans to bid for EU funding for large AI computing sites, heise online reports.

slides.title: A 30 billion euro target
body: The EU's InvestAI initiative wants to mobilise **over 30 billion euros** for AI gigafactories: at least 20 billion private, up to 10 billion public. That is a target, not money already committed.

slides.title: Three countries, one plan
body: The plan spans **Oulu in Finland, Iru in Estonia and Valmiera in Latvia**. A fourth site in Sweden is not yet decided, heise reports.

slides.title: Cold climate, spread-out risk
body: Spreading across countries lowers **concentration risk**, adds resilience and allows flexible expansion, per heise. The cool climate cuts cooling needs, and the region offers reliable renewable energy.

slides.title: Network, cloud and power
body: Nokia supplies the secure network, Nscale (a cloud provider) the training and inference platforms, Skeleton the power systems. Telia and its unit Cygate handle network and data transmission. Research partners are Finland's **VTT** and Sweden's **KTH**.

slides.title: Telekom is a rival
body: EuroHPC, the EU body running the tender, funds up to **four medium-sized and three large** AI gigafactories. Deutsche Telekom, with its Munich AI site, is among the most prominent competitors, heise reports.

facts.text: Five companies (5): Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda formed a consortium, AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), which plans to bid for EU AI gigafactory funding.
The EU's InvestAI wants to mobilise more than 30 billion euros for AI gigafactories, at least 20 billion euros private and up to 10 billion euros public.
EuroHPC Joint Undertaking funding covers up to four medium-sized and three large AI gigafactories.
Planned sites are Oulu (Finland), Iru (Estonia) and Valmiera (Latvia); the Swedish site is not yet decided.
Spreading across countries is meant to lower concentration risk, improve resilience and allow flexible expansion; the cool climate cuts cooling needs and renewable energy is reliable.
Nokia provides the secure network, Nscale cloud platforms for training and inference, Skeleton power systems; Telia and its subsidiary Telia Cygate provide network, data transmission and integration.
Research partners are VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and Sweden's KTH.
Deutsche Telekom is among the most prominent competitors for the funding.

sources.title_en: AI Gigafactory in the North: Nokia and partners plan European AI infrastructure

caption:
Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda want a Nordic and Baltic AI gigafactory, and they plan to bid for EU funding.

The group, AI Gigafactory Northern, plans sites in Finland, Estonia and Latvia, plus Sweden (site undecided), heise online reports. Deutsche Telekom is among the most prominent competitors.

→ The EU's InvestAI wants to mobilise over 30 billion euros for AI gigafactories; that is a target, not committed money
→ Planned sites: Oulu (Finland), Iru (Estonia), Valmiera (Latvia)
→ Why the north: cool climate, reliable renewable energy, lower concentration risk

Should Europe's AI compute sit in the cold north?

Source: heise online, "AI Gigafactory in the North: Nokia and partners plan European AI infrastructure" (in German), Nov 18, 2026.
